dial.summary: Risk Off persists on the eve of the Sep 15–16 FOMC decision, with 10Y TIPS real yields confirmed at 2.55% (headwind, +16bps 4-week rise), high probability of a hike from CME FedWatch, and BTC dominance recovering to 57.9% after the Sep 13 dip to 56.49%; TOTAL crypto at $2.69T and stablecoin dominance at 11.4% continues its 30-day decline, but the synchronized ECB–FOMC–BOE–BOJ tightening cluster (Sep 10–18) keeps macro headwinds intact.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) estimated at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; 6–8 week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); MacroMicro confirmed June 2026 G4 M2 at $102.66T; separate data confirms +12.05% YoY G4 M2 growth as of February 2026 with $101T in top-4 central bank M2; 4-week uptrend confirmed (June $102.66T → July ~$103.4T = +$0.74T, above flat threshold); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); synchronized global central bank tightening cluster (ECB hike Sep 10, FOMC Sep 16, BOE Sep 17, BOJ Sep 18) will apply modest G4 M2 headwinds via higher reserve costs and reduced asset purchases through Q4 2026, but the July aggregate remains the most recent confirmed reading.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp vs July), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp (no new ISM release until October 1); status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); FOMC Sep 16 hike would add financing-cost pressure to manufacturing capex; S&P Global Flash PMI Sep 23 will provide the next advance manufacturing-sector read before ISM October 1.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.65 on September 14, 2026 (Monday open; recovered from 99.09 close on September 11 as dollar firmed ahead of FOMC Sep 16); 4-week trend flat: ~99.60 (Aug 14, per Barchart mid-August technical analysis) → 99.65 (Sep 14) = +0.05%, well below the 0.5% flat threshold; trend shifts from 'down' to 'flat' as prior 4-week decline fully retraced; status neutral (ICE DXY 99.65 within 97.5–100 neutral band); FOMC Sep 16 hike + hawkish dot plot would test the 100 headwind threshold; BOJ Sep 18 is the primary downside DXY risk via potential yen carry unwind; DXY ranged 98.73–101.73 in August 2026 with the 52-week range at 95.55–101.80.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 confirmed at 2.55% on September 10, 2026 (H.15); 10Y nominal on September 11 reached 4.98% with implied 10Y breakeven of ~2.43%, consistent with DFII10 remaining near 2.55%; 4-week trend up: ~2.39% (Aug 11) → 2.55% (Sep 10) = +16bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% threshold both met); 10Y nominal at 4.98% approaching the psychologically significant 5% level; FOMC Sep 16 hike would extend real yield headwind as 10Y nominal is repriced higher while inflation expectations stay elevated at 2.4%+; next H.15 DFII10 observation for Sep 12 scheduled for release Sep 15.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 11, 2026 close: 10Y 4.98%, 2Y 4.63%, spread = +0.35% (+35bps); 2Y surged +24bps on Sep 11 following hot Aug CPI (+3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM) driving high FOMC hike probability; 4-week trend flat: ~+35bps (Aug 12) → +35bps (Sep 11) = 0bp change over 30 days, within flat threshold; status neutral (positive spread, not steepening; shifted from +0.34% to +0.35% on revised settlement data; supportive requires positive AND steepening); FOMC Sep 16 hike would further compress 2s10s as the 2Y prices above current levels while the 10Y is bounded by slowing growth expectations; spread remains structurally positive following the curve's uninversion earlier in 2026.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.74T for week ending September 10, 2026 (H.4.1 released September 11); prior week (Sep 3) also ~$6.74T and week ending Sep 2 at ~$6.70T; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 13) → $6.74T (Sep 10) = +$40B, within flat threshold; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; routine measured QT continues with no acceleration and no overnight rate spike); the +$135B year-over-year increase in WALCL as of September 2026 reflects the partial reversal of QT enacted in H1 2026; FOMC Sep 16 decision will inform any policy shift on balance sheet normalization pace.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately +0.01% per 8h (carried forward from September 9, 2026 confirmed read; direct Coinglass access unavailable from current environment); BTC at $77,453 on September 14 (+0.4% 24h), recovering from Sep 13 volatility; BTC dominance rebounded to 57.9% after the Sep 13 intraday dip to 56.49%; 30-day trend flat: near-zero throughout August–September 2026; well below the +0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding confirms spot-driven price action, not leveraged-long crowding); TOTAL crypto market at $2.69T.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$307B (September 14, 2026; CoinGecko); total crypto market cap $2.69T (−0.9% on the day); stablecoin dominance 11.4% ($307B / $2.69T); 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% in early August 2026 → 11.4% (Sep 14) = sustained ~2–3pp decline over 30 days confirming capital deployment into risk assets; the marginal uptick from 11.2% (Sep 13) to 11.4% reflects TOTAL contraction (not stablecoin supply expansion) as crypto fell to $2.69T from $2.74T; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply: TOTAL fell while dominance ticked marginally up); USDT leads stablecoin supply at $183.4B (60.6% share) followed by USDC at $74.2B.

upcoming.title: Empire State Manufacturing Survey (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Empire State Manufacturing Business Conditions Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — one of the earliest September manufacturing reads, released on FOMC Day 1 (two-day meeting Sep 15–16); August 2026 survey showed prices paid surging to 58.6 (from 52.3 in July), signaling cost-push inflation from Middle East energy spillover; a strong September reading would reinforce the ISM-above-50 expansion backdrop (54.6 in August) heading into the FOMC decision tomorrow; a sharp decline would raise questions about manufacturing sustainability despite robust ISM Production at 58.3%.

upcoming.title: FOMC Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve FOMC rate decision at 2:00 PM ET (two-day meeting Sep 15–16), press conference at 2:30 PM ET; includes updated Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) with dot plot; current target range 3.5%–3.75%; market-implied hike probability is high (CME FedWatch) following Aug CPI +3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM (Sep 11), Aug PPI +5.4% YoY (Sep 10), and Aug NFP +162K (Sep 4); dot plot and 2027 rate path guidance are the primary DXY, real yield, and risk-asset drivers for Q4 2026; a hike + hawkish dots would push 10Y above 5% and real yields above 2.60%, extending the headwind for risk assets including crypto.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Monthly Retail Sales for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released same day as FOMC decision (2:00 PM ET); prior July advance retail sales were +0.1% MoM; strong Aug NFP (+162K) suggests continued consumer income growth supporting spending; a strong retail sales print (+0.3% MoM or above) confirms Q3 consumer resilience and may reinforce the Fed's inflation-fighting case; a weak print (below 0%) would suggest consumer fatigue despite labor market strength, potentially complicating the FOMC policy calculus.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Board Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization for August 2026 at 9:15 AM ET — released same day as FOMC decision; measures output of manufacturing, mining, and utilities; a strong reading would reinforce ISM Manufacturing's expansion signal (54.6 in August); capacity utilization approaching 80% would add to inflationary pressures and potentially reinforce the FOMC hike case; watch energy sector output given diesel prices surging +24.1% MoM in August (Aug PPI, Sep 10).

upcoming.title: Bank of England Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee rate decision at 12:00 PM London time (7:00 AM ET) — one day after FOMC Sep 16; BOE has held Bank Rate at 3.75% since December 2025 (five consecutive holds); MPC voted 6-3 at July 30 meeting to hold, with Pill, Greene and Mann dissenting in favor of a hike to 4.00%; with ECB having hiked Sep 10 (to 2.50% deposit rate) and FOMC expected to hike Sep 16, a BOE hold with dovish guidance would create significant monetary policy divergence; market pricing implies roughly a one-in-three chance of a quarter-point hike to 4.00%.

upcoming.title: Housing Starts & Building Permits (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Housing Starts and Building Permits for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — a leading indicator for residential construction activity; released same day as BOE decision and Philadelphia Fed; higher rates (FOMC hiking Sep 16 at high probability) weigh on housing affordability; a decline in starts or permits would add to evidence that elevated financing costs are cooling the housing sector; 30Y fixed mortgage rates have been elevated in the 6.5–7.5% range throughout 2026.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Survey (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — a leading indicator for national ISM Manufacturing (next release Oct 1); released alongside Housing Starts and Initial Jobless Claims one day after the FOMC decision; a strong Philly Fed print reinforces the ISM-above-50 expansion backdrop; September business-sentiment reaction to the Sep 16 rate decision may begin to show in forward-looking orders and capex components; August 2026 survey showed elevated prices paid consistent with ISM trends.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 13, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 13, 2026 — first labor market read post-FOMC Sep 16; any significant spike above 220K would amplify rate-path repricing following the FOMC decision; prior weeks were approximately 206K; released alongside BOE rate decision, Housing Starts, and Philly Fed — a dense data morning one day after the FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: Bank of Japan Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting September 17–18, with Statement on Monetary Policy expected September 18 (midday Tokyo time, ~3:30 AM ET) — two days after FOMC Sep 16 and one day after BOE Sep 17; BOJ holds at 1.00% (held July 31 by 8-1 vote; member Takata proposed hike to 1.25%); BOJ warned core inflation could exceed 2% target from September onward; any surprise hike or hawkish commentary would strengthen JPY and potentially trigger yen-carry-trade unwinds with broad impact on global risk assets including crypto; DXY at 99.65 (neutral) — a hawkish BOJ would accelerate dollar weakness toward the 97.5 supportive threshold.
